utterances.text: Thank you, Micah. And good evening, Mayor and City Council. I'm Alexis Captanian, Housing Manager for the City of San Rafael, and tonight I am presenting an urgency ordinance for your consideration. The proposed ordinance would provide temporary relocation assistance and a right of return for tenants in the Canal Opportunity Zone who are displaced from their unit due to substantial rehabilitation for health and safety. So a little bit of background. In 2017, the tax cuts and Jobs Acts created tax incentives for investment in federally designated economically distressed census tracts called Opportunity Zones. To qualify for the program, a property that is acquired in the Opportunity Zone must be substantially improved over a 30 month period, a requirement that increases the risk of displacement for residential tenants due to no fault evictions. San Rafael currently has one Opportunity Zone comprised of two census tracts in the Canal neighborhood. The Opportunity Zone is shown in green light green on this map. There are approximately 1800 units in the opportunity zone and about 1500 are apartment units, giving the Opportunity Zone a much higher proportion of renters compared to the rest of the city. The Opportunity Zone has much higher rates of severe housing cost burden and overcrowding compared to the rest of San Rafael and Marin County. In March 2021, the City Council adopted an ordinance requiring property owners to pay relocation assistance to tenants evicted in the Opportunity Zone for substantial rehabilitation. Since October 2022, city staff has reviewed permanent relocation payments for 31 tenant households who were evicted on the grounds of substantial rehabilitation for health and safety within the Canal Opportunity Zone. Additionally, the city processed permit applications for another 37 units in the Opportunity Zone where the property owner indicated that a no fault eviction did not occur. By comparison, in the year and a half prior to that, the city did not review any relocation payments in the Opportunity Zone. Due to the tight rental market in San Rafael and Marin county, it is extremely difficult for displaced tenants tenants to secure other housing. Staff has received reports of displaced Opportunity Zone tenants moving out of Marin, doubling up with other families or becoming unhoused and moving into their cars. San Rafael's 2023 through 2031 housing element and the City Council's goals and objectives direct staff to conduct stakeholder engagement and evaluate citywide tenant protection policies. And staff is working on data collection and planning community engagement for this effort. The proposed Urgency Ordinance, which is specific to the Canal Opportunity Zone, is an interim measure to prevent further displacement of families due to substantial rehabilitation while the city undergoes this broader process regarding citywide tenant protection policies so the proposed ordinance temporarily amends an existing San Rafael policy called Cause Required for Eviction, which regulates the grounds for eviction in properties with three or more dwelling units. Under the current policy, a property owner can evict a tenant to perform substantial repairs. If this happens, the property owner is required to pay the tenant a relocation assistance payment, but the tenant does not have a right to return to the unit when the repairs are completed. The proposed Urgency ordinance amends the existing policy for the Opportunity Zone only, removing substantial rehabilitation as a cause for eviction. In most cases, the proposed ordinance would require property owners to offer tenants the right to return to their unit after repairs are completed. If the tenant wants to return to the unit after repairs are completed, the tenant must continue to pay rent while the unit is being repaired. In order to maintain the existing lease while the unit is being repaired, the landlord must either pay the tenant a daily amount to cover the cost of temporary lodging or the landlord has the option to provide a comparable unit on the property or another property in San Rafael. If the tenant does not want to be temporarily relocated and returned to the unit following repairs, the tenant can choose to move out permanently and is eligible for a Permanent Relocation Assistance payment, which already exists under city policy. This policy would be in effect through December 31, 2026, in line with the expiration of the Opportunity Zone tax benefits. The package under consideration tonight also includes a resolution specifying payment amounts. The daily temporary relocation payments proposed are $250 per day during the first 29 days of displacement based on the cost of hotel, motel and short term rental options in Marin county and then starting on day 30, the payment would be based on either the tenant's monthly lease rent or the current fair market rent, whichever is greater. So, for example, the 2024 fair market rent for a two bedroom is $3,359, so the daily payment would be about $112. The proposed ordinance requires staff review of relocation plans during the permitting process, and so the resolution proposes an administrative fee based on the fully burdened rate of the staff. Reviewer so to recap, the Urgency Ordinance would amend municipal code chapter 10.105, which is the cause required for eviction policy. It would also amend municipal code chapter 10.111, which is the Relocation Assistance and Opportunity zones The Permanent Relocation Assistance Assistance. And then the resolution would establish temporary relocation assistance, payment amounts and an administrative processing fee. And this policy would be in effect through December 31, 2026, in the Canal Opportunity Zone. The City Council has the following options to consider. Adopt the urgency ordinance and resolution. Adopt the urgency ordinance and resolution with modifications. Direct staff to return with more information or take no action. I'm joined by Director Micah Hinkle, and we are available to take your questions.

utterances.text: And I'm presenting for your consideration an Amendment to Resolution 15244 authorizing the use of previously awarded affordable Housing Trust funds for the renovation of units in an additional building at Marin Villa Estates. Canal alliance owns 12 affordable rental units in the three buildings at Marin Villa Estates in San Rafael's Canal neighborhood. These buildings, these building addresses are 153161 and 165 Nevada street and the units within them have not been updated and in over 20 years. In 2023, Canal alliance applied for a $400,000 grant from the city's Affordable Housing Trust Fund to renovate units in 161 and 165 Nevada Street. City Council authorized a grant of $200,000 from the housing and Lufy Fund for this project. City Council's original authorization of funds was only for buildings 161 and 165 Nevada street street. Canal alliance now requests to instead use the awarded funds to renovate three units located in their in their third building at Marin Villa Estates, which is 153 Nevado Street. The units at 153 Nevado street are equally in need of renovation and are deed restricted for households earning very low or low income. Canal Alliance's request does not seek additional funds for the proposed renovation, but proposes renovating three units instead of four, considering increase per unit expenditures due to rises in material and labor costs, including the application of prevailing wage requirements and in addition, asbestos inspection and abatement costs. The proposed use of funds would help preserve affordable housing and meets the evaluation criteria for the notice of funding availability and the city's guidelines for the administration of the Affordable Housing Trust Fund. The project remains consistent with the city's housing element goals to ensure housing habitability, maintenance and a diverse range of housing options throughout the city. Tonight, staff recommends that City Council adopt the resolution to amend Resolution 15-44 to authorize the use of funds for renovating units in an additional building at Marin Villa Estates.
